verdict: PulteGroup sold fewer homes as higher mortgage rates sidelined buyers — revenue fell 10% to $4.0B and profit fell to $476M, though a richer mix of move-up and active-adult buyers held the home sale gross margin at 24.8%.

segments.name: Home sales
segments.note: Homes closed — 6,876 homes at an average price of $561,000. Closings fell 9% as higher mortgage rates stretched affordability.

segments.name: Land sales and other
segments.note: Selling surplus land and other homebuilding revenue — much smaller than the $53M a year ago.

segments.name: Financial services
segments.note: Mortgage and title services for PulteGroup buyers — an 85% mortgage capture rate, and $46M of pre-tax income.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling and back-office costs — $397M, or 10.3% of home sale revenues, roughly flat in dollars vs a year ago.

otherDetail: Other income of $20M, less a $3M equity loss from unconsolidated ventures — $17M net added to profit.

takeaways.title: Fewer homes closed
takeaways.text: Closings fell 9% to 6,876 homes and the average price slipped 1% to $561,000, so home sale revenue fell 9% to $3.9B. Net new orders also fell 6% to 6,208 homes.

takeaways.title: Margin held up thanks to buyer mix
takeaways.text: Home sale gross margin was 24.8%, down from 26.2% a year ago and including $26M of land impairments. More than 60% of sales are now higher-margin move-up and active-adult homes.

takeaways.title: The backlog still grew
takeaways.text: Backlog rose 4% to 10,298 homes worth $6.4B, and PulteGroup ended the quarter with $1.4B of cash and a low 12% debt-to-capital ratio after buying back $350M of shares.

oneTimers: $26M of land impairments are inside home sale cost of revenues this quarter — about 0.7 percentage points of the reported 24.8% home sale gross margin.
